questions.stem: An ideal gas is enclosed in a cylinder at pressure of $2$ atm and temperature, $300$ K. The mean time between two successive collisions is $6 \times 10^{-8}$ s. If the pressure is doubled and temperature is increased to $500$ K, the mean time between two successive collisions will be close to:
questions.solution:
$t \propto \dfrac{\text{Volume}}{\text{velocity}}$, volume $\propto \dfrac{T}{P}$, velocity $\propto \sqrt{T}$

$$\frac{t_1}{6\times10^{-8}} = \frac{\sqrt{500}}{2P}\times\frac{P}{\sqrt{300}} \Rightarrow t_1 = 3.8\times10^{-8} \approx 4\times10^{-8}\ \text{s}$$

A stone is thrown vertically upward. On its way up it passes point $A$ with speed of $v$, and point $B$, $3$ m higher than A, with speed $\frac{v}{2}$. The maximum height reached by stone above point B is:
questions.solution:
$\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)^2 = v^2 - 2g\times3 \quad \therefore v = \sqrt{8g}$

If $h$ is the further height, then

$$0 = \left(\frac{v}{2}\right)^2 - 2gh \;\Rightarrow\; h = \frac{v^2}{8g} = \frac{8g}{8g} = 1\ \text{m}$$

questions.stem: A light wave is incident normally on a glass slab of refractive index $1.5$. If $4\%$ of light gets reflected and the amplitude of the electric field of the incident light is $30$ V/m, then the amplitude of the electric field for the wave propagating in the glass medium will be:
questions.solution:
$P_{refracted} = \dfrac{96}{100}P_I \Rightarrow K_2A_t^2 = \dfrac{96}{100}K_1A_i^2$

$\Rightarrow r_2A_t^2 = \dfrac{96}{100}r_1A_i^2 \Rightarrow A_t^2 = \dfrac{96}{100}\times\dfrac{1}{3/2}\times(30)^2$

$$A_t = \sqrt{\frac{64}{100}\times(30)^2} = 24$$

questions.stem: A block kept on a rough inclined plane, as shown in the figure, remains at rest up to a maximum force $2$ N down the inclined plane. The maximum external force up the inclined plane that does not move the block is $10$ N. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the plane is: [Take $g = 10\ \text{m/s}^2$]
questions.solution:
From figure, $2 + mg\sin30^\circ = \mu mg\cos30^\circ$ and $10 = mg\sin30^\circ + \mu mg\cos30^\circ$

Adding and subtracting: $\mu mg\cos30^\circ = 6$ and $mg\sin30^\circ = 4$. Dividing, $\dfrac{3}{2} = \mu\sqrt3$

$\therefore$ Coefficient of friction, $\mu = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$
questions.notes: Figure (incline 30°, 2 N down, 10 N up) appears only in the solution in the source.

questions.stem: A Carnot engine operating between temperatures $T_1$ and $T_2$ has efficiency $0.2$. When $T_2$ is reduced by $50$ K, its efficiency increases to $0.4$. Then $T_1$ and $T_2$ are respectively
questions.solution:
$\eta = 1 - \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} \Rightarrow 0.2 = 1 - \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} \Rightarrow \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = 0.8 \quad \ldots(i)$

When $T_2$ is reduced by 50 K: $0.4 = 1 - \dfrac{T_2 - 50}{T_1} \Rightarrow \dfrac{T_2-50}{T_1} = 0.6 \quad \ldots(ii)$

Dividing (i) by (ii): $\dfrac{T_2}{T_2-50} = \dfrac{4}{3} \Rightarrow T_2 = 200$ K

From (ii), $T_1 = \dfrac{200-50}{0.6} = 250$ K

When $M_1$ gram of ice at $-10^\circ$C (specific heat $= 0.5\ \text{cal g}^{-1}\,{}^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$) is added to $M_2$ gram of water at $50^\circ$C, finally no ice is left and the water is at $0^\circ$C. The value of latent heat of ice, in $\text{cal g}^{-1}$ is

questions.stem: For a prism kept in air it is found that for an angle of incidence $60^\circ$, the angle of prism A, angle of deviation $\delta$ and angle of emergence $e$ become equal. Then the refractive index of the material of prism is
questions.solution:
Given $i = 60^\circ$ and $A = \delta = e$.

$\delta = i + e - A \Rightarrow \delta = i \quad (\because e = A)$

Here angle of deviation is minimum ($\because i = e$).

$$\therefore \mu = \frac{\sin\left(\frac{60^\circ+60^\circ}{2}\right)}{\sin\frac{60^\circ}{2}} = 1.73$$

questions.stem: Two parallel plate capacitors X and Y have the same area of plates and same separation between plates. X has air and Y with dielectric of constant $2$ between its plates. They are connected in series to a battery of $12$ V. The ratio of electrostatic energy stored in X and Y is
questions.solution:
Same $A$, same $d$, same $Q$ (series).

$C_x = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0A}{d}$, $C_y = \dfrac{2\varepsilon_0A}{d}$; $U_x = \dfrac{Q^2}{2C_x}$, $U_y = \dfrac{Q^2}{2C_y}$

$$\therefore \frac{U_x}{U_y} = \frac{C_y}{C_x} = \frac{2}{1}$$

questions.stem: Two vibrating strings of the same material but lengths $L$ and $2L$ have radii $2r$ and $r$ respectively. They are stretched under the same tension. Both the strings vibrate in their fundamental modes, the one of length $L$ with frequency $f_1$ and the other with frequency $f_2$. The ratio $\dfrac{f_1}{f_2}$ is given by :-
questions.solution:
$f = \dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$, $\mu = \rho\pi r^2$

$$\frac{f_1}{f_2} = \frac{L_2}{L_1}\cdot\frac{r_2}{r_1} = \frac{2L}{L}\cdot\frac{r}{2r} = 1$$

questions.stem: Some liquid is filled in a cylindrical vessel of radius $R$. Let $F_1$ be the force applied by the liquid on the bottom of the cylinder. Now the same liquid is poured into a vessel of uniform square cross-section of side $R$. Let $F_2$ be the force applied by the liquid on the bottom of this new vessel. (Neglect atmosphere pressure) Then
questions.solution:
$\pi R^2h_1 = R^2h_2 \Rightarrow \pi h_1 = h_2$

$$\frac{F_1}{F_2} = \frac{\rho gh_1\times\pi R^2}{\rho gh_2\times R^2} = \frac{\pi h_1}{h_2} = 1$$

questions.stem: The displacement-time graphs for two sound waves A and B are shown in the figure, then the ratio of their intensities $I_A/I_B$ is equal to :-

questions.stem: The cathode of a photoelectric cell is changed such that the work function changes from $W_1$ to $W_2$ $(W_2 > W_1)$. If the current before and after change are $I_1$ and $I_2$, all other conditions remaining unchanged, then (assuming $h\nu > W_2$)
questions.solution: The work function has no effect on current so long as $h\nu > W_0$. The photoelectric current is proportional to the intensity of light. There is no change in the intensity of light, therefore $I_1 = I_2$.

questions.solution:
Since the leaving group breaks away as a base, it is easier to displace weaker bases than stronger bases. The basic strength of the given groups is in the order $\text{I}^- < \text{Br}^- < \text{Cl}^-$.

In the following series of reactions identify the major products A & B respectively.

Bromobenzene $\xrightarrow{\text{SO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4}$ A (major product) $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{Fe}}$ B (major product)
questions.solution:
Bromobenzene undergoes sulphonation at the para position (major) to give 4-bromobenzenesulfonic acid (A). Bromination then occurs ortho to Br and meta to $\text{SO}_3\text{H}$, giving 3,4-dibromobenzenesulfonic acid (B).

Both reactions are electrophilic substitutions: first sulphonation, then halogenation. –Br is o-/p-directing and gives the para product, while $\text{SO}_3\text{H}$ is meta directing; their cumulative directive influence gives B.

questions.stem:
For much of human history, silence was not regarded merely as the absence of sound. It was a deliberate condition in which thought could mature without constant interruption. Monasteries, libraries, and secluded study rooms were designed around this principle, recognising that sustained attention often requires a temporary withdrawal from the noise of ordinary life. Modern societies, however, increasingly treat silence as an uncomfortable void that must be filled with conversation, entertainment, or digital stimulation.
Yet silence can perform a function that noise cannot. It allows individuals to notice subtle distinctions, reconsider habitual assumptions, and listen to thoughts that might otherwise remain submerged beneath continual stimulation. This does not mean that silence is inherently superior to speech or activity. Excessive withdrawal can itself become unproductive, and meaningful dialogue is indispensable to intellectual development. The issue, therefore, is not whether one should choose silence over sound, but whether one possesses the freedom to choose between them.
In an environment saturated with competing demands for attention, the ability to remain silent may consequently represent something more significant than personal preference. It may be an exercise in intellectual autonomy—the capacity to determine what deserves one's attention rather than allowing external stimuli to determine it automatically.

What does the passage primarily suggest about the value of silence?

options.text: Silence is essential for intellectual development and should replace frequent communication.
Silence is mainly valuable because it protects individuals from technological distractions.
Silence is superior to speech because it enables people to develop independent opinions.
Silence can create conditions for reflection and focused thought when consciously chosen.

questions.stem:
In each question below, given two statements followed by four conclusions numbered I to IV. Consider the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts. Determine which conclusions logically follow from the given statements.

**Statement:**
All roads are bricks.
Some bricks are ropes.
All ropes are doors.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some roads are doors.
II. Some doors are bricks.
III. Some roads are not doors.
IV. All doors are ropes.

options.text: Only I, II and III follow.
Either I or III and II follow.
Either I or III and IV follow.

questions.solution:
From the Venn diagram: I – possible only; II – follows (some bricks are ropes, all ropes are doors); III – possible only; IV – does not follow.

I and III form a complementary pair, so either I or III follows, and II follows.
